gen-luckiest-guy-gf-khula: Loud, cheerful, poured-ink lettering from Luckiest Guy. Khula brings a generous midsection and curves that stay open, so the heading's ruler-drawn constant-width shout is followed by easy, unhurried text.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-krub: Krub keeps a pronounced x-height and curves that never quite close. Below Luckiest Guy, whose line has the flat look of fineliner on paper, paragraphs would glide along with plenty of open room inside each letter.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-miriam-libre: Luckiest Guy looks poured, every stroke a loud, cheerful ribbon of ink. Miriam Libre brings wire-drawn weight and a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, and that sturdiness is what makes the two get along.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-mozilla-text: Luckiest Guy is pure cheer, loud and poured. It is built to grab the eye from a distance, while Mozilla Text does its work up close, with big lowercase bodies and terminals that flare outward.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam keeps its curve endings well apart and its c, s and z full. Noto Sans Adlam keeps paragraphs open and clean beneath Luckiest Guy, whose diagonals carry exactly the weight of its uprights.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy matches its horizontals to its verticals in weight. And Noto Sans Arabic, with its wide openings and pronounced x-height, gives that loudness a clean, modern place to land.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Every curve in Luckiest Guy carries the weight of a straight stem, giving it a poured, loud, cheerful look. Noto Sans Armenian handles the quieter job, with full, inviting round letters.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Big, bright and drawn like a technical pen, Luckiest Guy shouts while Noto Sans Avestan keeps its curve tips apart. One brings the noise, the other brings clear, uncluttered space.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Luckiest Guy lays down loud, cheerful strokes with the steadiness of a drawn string. Noto Sans Bassa Vah counters with a dominant midsection and an open-jawed c like pliers, and both fonts clearly mean business.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-batak: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy looks marker-traced, while Noto Sans Batak towers on a stubby pencil-stroke x-height. Both stay friendly, because the body's wide-open e never looks squeezed shut.
